subject: Potential third‑party IP claim — notice, evidence request, and MSA scope sequencing
messages:
From: Mike Adams <mike.adams@acme-analytics.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Bethany Cole <bethany@lexbridge-legal.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Notice of potential IP claim / request for MSA defense allocation

Olga —

Quick heads up: our security team flagged a customer support ticket that alleges a third‑party patent may have been infringed by outputs generated during a paid evaluation last quarter. We are early in triage but need to get Redwood's contractual position and evidence requests in motion to satisfy our board and procurement timelines.

Please confirm: 1) whether Redwood will accept defense ("defend and hold harmless") for third‑party IP claims under the current proposed MSA language; 2) what evidence we should collect and the delivery cadence; and 3) whether there are carveouts you anticipate (e.g., model‑output only limitations, open‑source training data exceptions).

I attached the customer notice packet and the initial support trace. Bethany is on copy and will coordinate legal intake. We need to get your redline back to procurement this week if possible.

Attachments: Acme_notice_packet.pdf (15 KB), support_trace.txt (log snippet)

Thanks,
Mike
Director, Procurement
Acme Analytics

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Mike Adams <mike.adams@acme-analytics.com>, Bethany Cole <bethany@lexbridge-legal.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Notice of potential IP claim / request for MSA defense allocation

Mike / Bethany —

Thanks for the notice and for sending the packet. Short answers up front: under our current standard MSA the vendor (Redwood) accepts defense for third‑party IP claims subject to the usual conditions (timely notice, sole defense/control, cooperation). That said, we are proposing several narrowings in the order form / MSA to address exposure from model outputs and training data.

What we need from Acme now to move quickly:
- A CSV manifest of the specific prompts/outputs at issue (timestamps recommended).
- The customer support ticket thread and any customer communications to the claimant.
- Confirmation whether Acme used any private customer data in the experiments that produced the outputs.

Attached: evidence_manifest.csv (template) and our current redline (redlines_MSA_v3.docx). Highlights in the redline:
- Carveout language limiting Redwood's indemnity for claims that arise solely from customer modifications to prompts or from customer‑provided data that was never inspected by Redwood engineers.
- A rebuttable presumption path for claims tied to model hallucination vs. claims tied to trained‑in code artifacts.
- Proposed insurance offset and $2M cap for third‑party IP claims on the order form.

If Acme can push the manifest and the ticket by EOD Thursday (12/3), I will loop in Kimberly and Ben for contract posture and we will send a revised order form by Friday. If you prefer a short call to walk through redline tradeoffs, we can set one up.

[Attachment: redlines_MSA_v3.docx (Word doc, 48 KB)]

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: ACME — redline posture and negotiation script

Team — quick internal note so OLGA has a clear negotiation script for procurement. I read Olga's redline and I agree with the carveouts but propose the following negotiation priorities (we can present as fallbacks):

1) Primary ask: Keep defend obligation but narrow to claims "arising from the Model's outputs" and exclude claims resulting from (a) customer‑supplied data that was processed in a way Redwood did not control, and (b) customer alterations to prompt pipelines.

2) Escalator: If Acme insists on broader defend obligation, push for insurance offset language and a sublimit specific to third‑party IP with an explicit escrow / indemnity fund trigger at $250k retention.

3) Evidence and control: We must retain sole defense control. For discovery/evidence, Acme provides the manifest and all communications. We will agree to a 5‑day initial evidence window to triage.

4) Market signal: For enterprise deals at this scale we should offer a one‑time additional professional service (audit) to help produce the manifest — priced separately. Good sales lever.

I also recommend a short 30‑minute alignment call with Acme legal (Bethany) after they deliver the manifest; Kimberly, please prepare suggested redline paragraphs and include sample language for the escrow/insurance offset.

Ben
Senior Counsel, Customer Success & Contracts
[Internal note: I added Acme_notice_packet.pdf and evidence_manifest.csv to the shared folder]

From: Bethany Cole <bethany@lexbridge-legal.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Mike Adams <mike.adams@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Notice of potential IP claim / request for MSA defense allocation

Olga / Ben —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. Acme can deliver the manifest and the support ticket export by EOD Thursday (12/10). A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Acme will not sign anything that leaves the claimant without an operational remedy — so we need to avoid language that effectively punts on remediation obligations (e.g., if outputs are served to end users).
- On carveouts: Acme accepts exclusions for customer‑supplied data, but only if Redwood can demonstrate that the claimed harm is attributable to the customer's change. We expect Redwood to provide a short technical memo alongside defense acceptance documenting the causal chain.
- On defense control: Acme asks for weekly syncs during the first 60 days of triage so they can understand Redwood's remediation plan; they accept Redwood leading the defense but want transparency.

We will review the redlines in redlines_MSA_v3.docx and provide countered language in a DocuSign envelope if the commercial team agrees. In parallel, Acme will sign a statement of facts for the disclosed outputs so Redwood can run an internal forensics sweep.

DocuSign (candidate) and drive links posted here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cMSA-redlines-ACM087 and https://www.docusign.com/session/embeddedSigning?envelopeId=0f4a2b

Bethany Cole
Counsel, Lexbridge Legal (outside counsel to Acme Analytics)
[Attachment: Acme_notice_packet.pdf (15 KB)]
